content.overview: Section 128 requires every company to keep proper books of account and other relevant papers at its registered office, on accrual basis and double-entry system.
content.glance: Section 128 requires every company to keep proper books of account and other relevant papers at its registered office, on accrual basis and double-entry system.
content.study: Books must explain transactions, including at the registered office and branches, and give a true and fair view. They may be kept electronically in the manner prescribed. The default place is the registered office; another place in India needs a board resolution and intimation to the Registrar. Books of the preceding eight financial years, or such shorter life of the company, must be preserved. A director may inspect. Branch returns are sent periodically. Failure exposes managing director, whole-time director in charge of finance, CFO, and other persons charged by the board.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How long must books be preserved?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Eight financial years immediately preceding the current year, or the company's whole life if shorter.
